comment: Pinned toolchain of the beastmount.exe build (build/winpe/beastmountsrc.py): Ubuntu 26.04's MinGW-w64 cross compiler, as the exact .deb files. Each is checked against its SHA-256 and size before use (the values are those of the resolute main/universe Packages index, whose hash is in the archive-signed InRelease; apt-get download verified them on 2026-10-25), then unpacked with dpkg-deb -x into the cache and run from there, so every build uses the same compiler bytes. The snapshot URL is the same file, kept after the archive moves on. To update: new versions, sha256 and size from apt-cache show, the snapshot timestamp, and check that two builds still give the same bytes.
name: mingw-w64-toolchain
cflags_comment: -s: no symbols; --no-insert-timestamp: PE TimeDateStamp 0 (the only date in the image); win32 thread model, plain C: the program links only KERNEL32.dll and msvcrt.dll, both in every Windows PE
host_libs_comment: shared libraries the unpacked compiler (cc1, as, ld) loads from the host; any Ubuntu 26.04 with gcc has them. Without them the build runs in the docker image of build/grub/source.lock.json (apt snapshot), with these and dpkg
